definitions.explanation: A formal expression of apology that literally means 'there is no excuse.' Used to convey sincere remorse or regret for causing inconvenience or trouble to someone.

examples.japanese: ご{迷惑|めいわく}をおかけして{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません。
{遅|おく}れてしまい、{本当|ほんとう}に{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}なく{思|おも}っております。
examples.english: I am truly sorry for being late.

notes:
One of the most important apologetic expressions in Japanese, more formal than すみません and much more formal than ごめん. Literally means "there is no excuse" — the speaker acknowledges there is nothing they can say to justify what happened.

COMMON FORMS:
- {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ない: plain form (casual)
- {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ないです: polite form
- {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません: formal polite
- {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ございません: very formal/humble (business, customer service)
- {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}なく{思|おも}う: to feel sorry

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～して{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ない: sorry for doing ~
- ～で{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ない: sorry about ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- すみません: general-purpose apology, lighter and more versatile
- ごめんなさい: casual apology to someone of equal or lower status
- {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}ります: humble expression closer to "I'm afraid" or "excuse me" than a direct apology

USAGE:
Also written {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ない as one compound. Often used in business settings and customer service. Can also be used as a set phrase when declining something: {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありませんが... (I'm sorry, but...).
